scope: Original unreviewed online source metadata plus explicitly reviewed local source-labelled photos. Gallery expansion is separate from model training and laboratory accuracy.

RRUFF.citation: Lafuente, B., Downs, R. T., Yang, H., & Stone, N. (2015). The power of databases: the RRUFF project. Highlights in Mineralogical Crystallography, pp. 1–30.
RRUFF.photo_permission_conclusion: Public viewing/download and citation instructions observed; no explicit per-photo reuse license confirmed. Author and permission review required before acquisition or training.

Wikimedia Commons.photo_permission_conclusion: Each indexed file has its own author and license metadata. Verify file rights and comply with attribution, license and any other stated conditions before reuse.

local_photo_publication.scope: Only individually licensed, pixel/source/hash/group-reviewed photos are copied offline; other records remain unreviewed metadata.
local_photo_publication.training_ready_meaning: Eligible for source-labelled research training; does not mean a released model trained on every gallery photo.

taxonomy.notes: Use species names, with legacy model aliases retained only as mapping metadata. Varieties, groups, rocks and mineraloids are not counted as extra species.

identification_evidence.description_excerpt: Thomsonite-Ca , Analcime Locality: Skookumchuck Dam, Bucoda , Thurston County, Washington , USA ( Locality at mindat.org ) Size: 5.0 x 3.6 x 2.2 cm. Colorful, well-developed spheroids of pastel-orange, bladed thomsonite attractively cover the mounded matrix of sharp, glassy, colorless analcime crystals on this fine combination zeolite specimen from the Skookumchuck Dam locality of Washington. Crystallized thomsonite is rare from any locality compared to other zeolite species. Ex. Rice NW Museum Collection.
